title: Sunday · lockboxes
venue: Arthur's site · the coastal weeklies · from 2017 the aggregator
logline: Main street in July, every front door with a key safe on it, drawn one by one. The Airbnb summer as a landscape. Chloe's parents' old house has one.

panels.composition: Tier 1: a row of old wooden houses along the street in July sun, and on every door, a gray key lockbox, each drawn exactly, twelve of them.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rusted tin, a row of old wooden houses along a sunny small-town street with a small gray key lockbox on every front door, drawn precisely, no people, no words
image.notes: Twelve doors, twelve boxes. Count them.

panels.name: Doors

panels.composition: Tier 2: one door, close: the porch step, the door, the lockbox hanging from the knob, swinging slightly.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rusted tin, close on an old wooden front door with a gray key lockbox hanging from its knob and a worn porch step below, no words
image.notes: The porch from October 2000 (dw_2000-10). The strip doesn't say.

panels.name: Four doors down

panels.composition: Tier 3: the street from its end, all the doors, all the boxes, nobody home anywhere. Held.

image.prompt: wet-on-wet watercolor in gray-green moss, fog and rusted tin, a small-town street seen from its end with lockboxes on every door and nobody home, no words

panels.name: Street

art.line: razor-sharp brush and ink; the pup's weight learned; Sundays wet-on-wet
art.palette: dailies: ink and one tone. Sundays: gray-green, fog, rust, bruised dusk

notes: Twelve boxes. Her porch, four doors down, has one.
